newsitem.title: USA: Low use estimates add to oil product spikes-DOE.
newsitem.headline: Low use estimates add to oil product spikes-DOE.

text.p: A recent tendency to underestimate the world's growth in oil consumption may contribute to seasonal price spikes of petroleum products, an Energy Department official said Wednesday.

Energy Department senior policy advisor Kyle Simpson said underestimating demand growth -- caused partly because growing consumers such as China and India do not have sophisticated methods of assessing use -- may exacerbate tight supply situations, contributing to price spikes.

At a symposium on U.S. dependence on imported oil, Simpson also said the department is studying establishing a strategic reserve for petroleum products as part of its overall evaluation of the Strategic Petroleum Reserve that is to be completed this fall.
Simpson said there have been earlier studies on having a products reserve which have shown it would be too expensive, physically difficult to do, and could disrupt markets.

Unlike crude oil, products deteriorate in storage. If reserves were not used in case of weather or supply emergencies, the stocks would have to be returned to the market which could be disruptive, he said.
